acceptanceCriteria: Per-step timing breakdown of status_with_runtime's five readiness steps is recorded with a reproducible method (temporary, never-committed instrumentation with exact line citations and commands).

The dominant cost (historical_finalization_inventory) is attributed to a specific code path (resolve_resource_finalization_head re-scanning .ai/decisions per outer-loop item) with line citations, and the O(n^2) vs O(n) distinction is empirically supported, not assumed.
A control measurement against a freshly attached empty repository shows the same steps cost <1ms, isolating the cost to accumulated repository history rather than a fixed per-call cost.

A partial-reproduction experiment (real receipts without their archive companions) is reported honestly, including that it did not reproduce the full cost, to avoid overclaiming a simpler explanation than the evidence supports.
No Rust source, test, or governance file changes; cargo fmt/clippy/test --workspace remain unaffected from the current passing baseline.
A concrete, narrowly-scoped, semantics-preserving candidate fix is recommended for the next P1 Work Item, without implementing it here.
goal: Hand the next P1 optimization Work Item a verified, line-cited bottleneck instead of a guess: identify which of status's internal readiness steps dominates its cost, and why, using reproducible temporary profiling that is never committed.
intent: Root-cause, with reproducible evidence, why ai-cockpit status is ~20-40x slower than inspect/doctor/observe on this repository, before any optimization is attempted (P0 bottleneck ranking).
outOfScope: Implementing any fix for the identified O(n^2) historical_finalization_inventory cost
phase instrumentation surfaced in CLI JSON output
or any other P0/P1 item not directly needed to attribute status's cost
